# Product Information (Brand-Blinded)

> Fixture for the T3 test suite. This describes a **fictional** product invented
> for testing. Any resemblance to a shipping device is coincidental — do not
> treat the review quotes below as real statements about any real product.

## Product Overview

[PRODUCT] is a wearable [CATEGORY] pendant that clips to a shirt collar and
records the wearer's day. [BRAND] positions it as "an effortless second memory
for people who are tired of taking notes." [S1] The pendant transcribes
conversations, summarizes them, and pushes a daily digest to a companion phone
app. [S1] Retail price is $329, with a required [FEATURE] plan at $19/month
after the first 30 days. [S1]

## Product Features and Capabilities

- Continuous audio capture with automatic speaker separation. [S1]
- "All processing happens on the device — your conversations never leave your
  possession." [S1]
- Daily summary digest delivered to the companion app each evening. [S1]
- Marketing copy describes the interaction model as "just tap once and forget
  it's there." [S1]
- The vendor states the feature set is "deliberately minimal — one button, one
  job." [S1]
- Reviewers note the concept is "essentially the same pitch as the wave of
  clip-on recorders that came before it." [S3]

## Technical Specifications

- Weight: 18 g. Housing is machined 6063 aluminium with a bead-blasted finish. [S2]
- Anodized in four colourways; the magnetic clasp is described by the vendor as
  "a satisfying click you'll fidget with." [S2]
- Battery: 240 mAh, rated for 12 hours of continuous capture. [S2]
- No display. A single RGB status LED indicates recording state. [S2]
- Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.2 to the companion app. No Wi-Fi radio. [S2]
- No edge AI chipset, NPU, or on-device model architecture is disclosed
  anywhere in the vendor's materials. [S2]
- The vendor says the housing is "built to survive being dropped on a sidewalk"
  and that units are "tested extensively before shipping." [S1]

## User Feedback & Reviews

- A hands-on review found that "the transcription — the entire point of the
  device — garbled roughly a third of what was said in any room with more than
  two people talking." [S3]
- The same review notes: "despite the on-device promise, pulling the phone into
  airplane mode stopped summaries from ever appearing, which tells you where the
  work is actually happening." [S3]
- A teardown write-up observes that "there is no accelerator of any kind on this
  board, just a Bluetooth SoC." [S4]
- One reviewer called the enclosure "a bit anonymous-looking for something you
  wear on your chest all day." [S3]
- Multiple owners report that setup is "confusing," with several noting they
  needed to retry pairing before the app recognised the pendant. [S5]
- Owners on a community forum report that "after about four months the clasp
  loosens enough that it slides off a collar on its own." [S5]
- A common complaint: "you have to open the companion app and leave it in the
  foreground before every session, or you get nothing." [S5]
- Another: "it needs charging every single night, which for a device whose whole
  pitch is that you forget about it is a real irony." [S5]
- One reviewer summarised it as "a second screen and a second radio strapped to a
  problem that a microphone already solved." [S3]
- A buyer's guide notes that "the free voice memo app already on your phone does
  the same recording and the same summary, immediately, for nothing." [S3]
- The same guide adds: "at $329 plus a subscription, you are paying flagship
  money for a feature whose accuracy nobody has been able to confirm." [S3]
- Coverage of the terms of service notes that "if you stop paying the monthly
  plan, the pendant stops transcribing entirely and becomes an inert clip." [S3]
- A market analysis observes that "the audience for always-on personal recording
  remains a narrow slice of knowledge workers rather than a general market." [S4]
- Overlap is flagged repeatedly: "most buyers already own two other devices that
  capture audio just as well." [S3]

## Policies & Support

- 30-day return window; the subscription is non-refundable once activated. [S1]
- One-year limited warranty on the housing. [S1]
